about: §22's durations shortened for live runs, so that every deadline a scenario can meet falls within an hour of the run's start; the windows over the history (user_gap, coverage, capacity, refusal) are an hour or less too. Every rule of §22 holds (Params::valid): lease.first <= lease.default <= lease.max <= lease.ceiling; presence.resolution <= presence.silence / 3; session.retain > lease.ceiling and > presence.silence; user_question.due_absent <= user_question.due; refusal.backoff <= refusal.ttl. Of the other orders among §22's defaults, those that shape what agents meet are kept: presence.silence = lease.first, so a session that vanished leaves present when its first lease ends; refusal.ttl, refusal.window, and archive.after > session.retain. Three are inverted, because the agents run at their real speed while the deadlines are compressed, and keeping them would cut a hold or a delivery below what a live agent needs: question.recheck < lease.max (keeping it means a recheck past 15 min, beyond the hour with two rechecks, or a lease.max under 6 min); user_question.due < lease.ceiling (keeping it means a ceiling under 15 min, which long live work reaches); deliver.window > user_question.due (keeping it means notes delivered for under 15 min). With the defaults too a recheck can fire during a hold renewed toward its ceiling, so the first inversion adds no new case. `harness/params.py` (ORDERS) checks all of this. The fixed values of §22 do not scale: a checkpoint is still due 5 minutes after a hold's issue or 1 minute before its lease ends, whichever is first.
